newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Copel begins roadshow for 8-yr bond.
newsitem.headline: Copel begins roadshow for 8-yr bond.

text.p: Brazil's Parana state power company Copel began a European roadshow for its $150 million eight-year, putable bond Tuesday, an official at lead manager Banco Santander said.
"The roadshow started today in Geneva and will later go to London and maybe Zurich," the official, who requested anonymity, said from New York.
The bond, Copel's first-ever Eurobond, is putable and callable at five years. It is not guaranteed by the federal government, the official said.
Salomon Brothers is also participating in the deal, he said.
Market players said the deal would likely be priced at between 270 and 290 basis points over five-year U.S. Treasuries, which could attract some attention.

"If it prices in this range it should do well," said one Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo. A recent uptick in the market and Brasilia's decision last night to raise electricity rates by close to 10 percent should help the Copel issue, market sources added.
